AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Pro Tem Garcia called the regular City Council meeting to order at 5:07 p.m. 

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any Closed Session items.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION The four members of the City Council and Successor Agency recessed to Closed Session at 5:09 p.m. Mayor Lainez was absent.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION All four members of the City Council and Successor Agency reconvened to open session at 6:03 p.m. 

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session stated that all four members of the Council were present, for items 1  and 2, staff provided presentations, the City Council gave directions, and no final reportable actions were taken.

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Pro Tem Garcia called the regular City Council meeting to order at 6:04 p.m. 

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Finance Director Castellon led the Pledge of Allegiance.

INVOCATION Mayor Pro Tem Garcia offered the invocation.

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

PUBLIC COMMENT Yvonne Sandoval thanked Parks and Recreation staff for supporting a recent community art event and acknowledged staff assistance during memorial activities for Elsie Cardoza. She requested that the City install a commemorative plaque on the desk of Elsie Cardoza at the Senior Center in her honor and for her service to the senior community.

Susana Larios spoke regarding the Modelo project and ongoing construction activities near her neighborhood. She described impacts from noise, vibrations, dust, and disruption to daily life and expressed concerns regarding health, safety, and quality of life for nearby residents.

Consondra Batiste expressed concerns regarding construction-related vibrations and alleged damage to residential properties near the Modelo project. She requested greater assistance and clarity from the City regarding what actions can be taken to protect affected homeowners.

Veronica Chavez addressed concerns regarding the Modelo project, including construction impacts, vibration monitoring, alleged property damage, project oversight, and environmental compliance issues. She requested release of vibration monitoring data and independent structural assessments for affected homes.

Mark Chavez discussed concerns regarding construction impacts on nearby residences, requested independent professional evaluations of affected properties, and sought greater transparency regarding vibration monitoring data and enforcement of developer commitments.

Leonard Mendoza commented on the City's handling of resident concerns related to the Modelo project and encouraged greater involvement between City officials, residents, and the developer. He also expressed opinions regarding City Council term limits and elected office tenure.

CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo

SCHEDULED MATTERS

7.. PRESENTATION/UPDATE FROM THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY IN THE CITY OF COMMERCE Sergeant Cortez provided a presentation on the public safety report for May 2026. The presentation included crime statistics, trends, and enforcement activity within the City. Overall crime levels remained comparable to recent months, with an increase noted in crimes against persons.

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Council Member Rebollo expressed appreciation for Council Member Altamirano’s vision in establishing the senior art program and reflected on attending the recent Senior Art Gala. She noted that witnessing the pride, talent, and accomplishments of the participating senior artists exceeded her expectations and highlighted the positive impact the program had on the participants and their families. She shared that the event demonstrated that it is never too late to discover and develop new talents and commended the artists for their dedication and achievements. 

Council Member Rebollo also congratulated all graduates in the community, from preschool through college, and offered special recognition to her son Daniel and his teammates as they advanced to high school and continued pursuing their water polo goals. Additionally, she attended Pedal Palooza and praised Parks and Recreation, Public Works, the Library, and all participating departments for delivering a successful community event. She highlighted the wide variety of activities, strong community participation, and collaboration among City departments that contributed to the event’s success.

Council Member Argumedo congratulated all graduates and reported attending Schurr High School’s graduation ceremony, where he celebrated his granddaughter’s achievement. He commended the school for its improvements and noted the strong attendance and enthusiasm displayed by graduates, families, and community members. He also recognized the accomplishments of the City’s Student Mayor and expressed pride in seeing local youth honored for their achievements.

Council Member Argumedo also attended Pedal Palooza and commended Parks and Recreation staff and volunteers for organizing a successful event. He highlighted the family-friendly atmosphere, community participation, and recreational activities, including pickleball, which he enjoyed experiencing firsthand. 

He also attended the Women in Business luncheon at the Commerce Casino and recognized Vanessa Haro, who was honored for her contributions to the community through youth martial arts programs. He commended her commitment to serving local youth and noted that her remarks were inspiring and well received.

Council Member Altamirano praised the success of Pedal Palooza and thanked Parks and Recreation staff, volunteers, and community partners for organizing the event. He highlighted the BMX demonstrations, instructional activities, bicycle raffles, and strong community participation. He further suggested exploring scholarship opportunities for residents pursuing careers in the skilled trades, including electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and other vocational fields. He acknowledged recent family birthdays and expressed appreciation for the support shown by the community.

Council Member Altamirano reflected on the success of the senior art program and art gallery, noting the pride and excitement displayed by participating artists. He shared that many of the senior artists developed a strong attachment to their work and discussed opportunities to create prints of the artwork to allow residents to purchase copies while preserving the original pieces. He commended the senior artists for their creativity and talent and expressed interest in expanding similar opportunities for youth participating in the City’s art programs. He concluded by noting the lasting impact the program had on participants and their families.

Mayor Pro Tem Garcia reported attending the Senior Art Gallery and congratulated all participating artists. She described the event as a tremendous success and praised the quality of the artwork and the positive impact the program had on participants. Inspired by the exhibit, she expressed interest in participating in future art classes. She also attended the Color Run and Pedal Palooza events and commended Parks and Recreation, Public Works, and City staff for providing a fun and engaging experience for residents of all ages. She highlighted the variety of recreational activities available throughout the event and noted the strong community participation.

Mayor Pro Tem Garcia further recognized staff for creating an engaging promotional video highlighting the City’s park programs and encouraged continued efforts to showcase recreational opportunities available to residents. She thanked Patty Barunda for coordinating transportation for the 10-and-under girls water polo team and acknowledged Social Services staff for their ongoing efforts to connect unhoused individuals with available resources and assistance.  Lastly, she thanked Bobby Contreras for organizing another successful Junior Olympic water polo qualifier tournament and requested that the City continue highlighting local water polo tournaments, teams, and accomplishments through its communication platforms to increase community awareness and recognition of youth achievements.

ADJOURNMENT There being no further business to come before the City Council, Mayor Pro Tem Garcia adjourned the meeting at 7:33 p.m.

Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings) in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California, and the Central Library, 5655 Jillson Street, Commerce, California.


Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.


6.. Community Facilities District (CFD) Education Finance Director Castellon introduced Brian Forbath and Dan Massiello, Kosmot consultants, that provided a summary on the CFD presentation. The presentation provided an overview of the purpose and legal framework of CFDs, financing mechanisms for public infrastructure improvements, the CFD formation process, landowner election requirements, bond financing procedures, and the roles of consultants and City staff in administering the district. Staff also presented a proposed timeline for future Council consideration. 

During Council discussion, several Council Members expressed interest in obtaining additional information and requested further discussions with staff to address questions and concerns before considering any future action. 

No action was taken, and the presentation was received and filed.

1.. 2026 Summer Reading Program “Plant a Seed, Read” Senior Librarian Sylvia Cisneros presented the Commerce Public Library's 2026 Summer Reading Program beginning June 15, 2026. The program includes reading challenges and activities for children, teens, and adults, with a focus on gardening, healthy eating, literacy, and hands-on educational experiences.

Council Members thanked Library staff for providing educational opportunities and community programming.
